# Restyle CdnPicker.vue with InstUI component classes

## Context

The CDN guide page (`docs/guide/cdn.md`) mounts an interactive combine-URL builder,
`CdnPicker.vue`. Today that component is styled with a bespoke `<style scoped>` block using
BEM class names (`.cdn-picker__*`) and raw VitePress theme variables (`--vp-c-*`). The docs
site already loads the full `@pantoken/components` sheet plus the utilities sheet in its theme
entry, so every `instui-*` class is available globally. The picker is the one interactive widget
on the CDN guide, and it currently looks like generic VitePress chrome rather than InstUI.

Goal: rebuild the picker's markup on the shipped InstUI component classes so it reads as an
InstUI surface — matching the look documented in `docs/guide/components.md` — while keeping all
existing behavior (selection state, combine-URL generation, copy, localized strings) unchanged.

## What's available (already loaded in the docs theme)

`docs/.vitepress/theme/index.ts` imports `generated/components.css` (the full component barrel,
including `instui-checkbox`, `instui-radio`, `instui-radio-input-group`, `instui-button`,
`instui-form-field-group`) and `formats/components/generated/utilities.css` (`instui-view`,
`instui-bg-*`, `instui-p-*`/`instui-m-*`, `instui-border-*`, `instui-elevation-*`,
`instui-text`, `instui-heading`). No new imports are needed — this is a template + scoped-CSS
edit only. Reference markup lives in `docs/guide/components.md`.

## Class mapping (behavior stays identical)

Single file: `docs/.vitepress/theme/components/CdnPicker.vue`. Only the `<template>` and
`<style scoped>` change; the `<script setup>` is untouched.

| Current | New |
| --- | --- |
| `.cdn-picker` container | `instui-view` + `instui-bg-secondary` + `instui-p-md` + `instui-border-radius-lg` + `instui-elevation-card` (a real InstUI view surface) |
| `.cdn-picker__group` `<fieldset><legend>` | `instui-form-field-group` (native fieldset/legend, InstUI-styled legend) |
| `.cdn-picker__all` + grid `<label class="cdn-picker__check">` | `<label class="instui-checkbox">` (control-first markup already matches) |
| token-sheet radios (lean/full) | `instui-radio-input-group -variant-toggle` wrapping `instui-radio -variant-toggle` — a segmented control **(pending your choice below)** |
| format radios (link/import) | same segmented `instui-radio-input-group -variant-toggle` **(pending your choice below)** |
| include-base checkbox | `instui-checkbox` (kept beside the format group) |
| `.cdn-picker__copy` button | `instui-button -size-small -color-secondary` |
| `.cdn-picker__note` | `instui-text -size-x-small -color-secondary` |
| `.cdn-picker__empty` | `instui-text -color-secondary -style-italic` |

### Residual scoped CSS (only what no utility covers)

Keep a small `<style scoped>` for genuine layout, dropping everything the classes now handle:

- `.cdn-picker__components` — the scrollable grid box: `grid-template-columns`,
  `gap`, `max-height`, `overflow-y`. Chrome (border/radius/padding/bg) moves to
  `instui-view instui-border instui-border-radius-md instui-p-sm`.
- disabled dimming on the grid when "all" is checked (keep the `--disabled` modifier rule, or
  swap for the `instui-opacity-disabled` utility + `pointer-events:none`).
- `.cdn-picker__options` — the flex row holding the two option groups.
- copy-button absolute positioning over the `<pre>` (button styling itself comes from
  `instui-button`).
- The code block `<pre><code>` stays as-is (VitePress code styling) unless we wrap the output
  area in `pantoken-prose` — see fork below.

## Verification

1. Start a preview server on a distinct port with `--strictPort` (do not reuse the user's).
   Example: `vpr docs:dev` equivalent bound to a free port; confirm the exact command against
   `docs/conventions/build-and-docs.md` before running.
2. Navigate to `/guide/cdn` (and one locale, e.g. `/hu/guide/cdn`) in the preview.
3. Verify with `preview_snapshot` / `preview_inspect`: the surface shows the InstUI card look,

4. Toggle light/dark via `preview_resize` colorScheme to confirm token-driven theming holds.
5. `preview_screenshot` for a before/after visual.

## What changed

Single file: [CdnPicker.vue](docs/.vitepress/theme/components/CdnPicker.vue) — template and scoped styles only; the `<script setup>` (state, combine-URL logic, copy, i18n) is untouched.

| Element | Now uses |

content.text:
Zero warnings and zero errors confirmed.

## Summary

The three warnings were pre-existing TypeDoc noise from the API-generation step, unrelated to the CDN picker change. They all came from one doc comment — the `register()` function in [renderers/web-components/src/index.ts:200](renderers/web-components/src/index.ts:200), which linked to `{@link ELEMENTS}` (exported) and `{@link NESTED_DEPS}` (a private, non-exported const). Angular re-exports `register` verbatim, so it inherited the same broken links.

Two-part fix:

1. **Source comment** — replaced the two `{@link …}` references with plain inline text. `NESTED_DEPS` is a private implementation detail that shouldn't be a doc link, and `ELEMENTS` reads fine as inline code.
2. **Rebuilt `@pantoken/web-components`** — angular resolves `register` from the package's built `dist/index.d.mts`, which still carried the old comment. Regenerating it (`node scripts/generate.ts && node scripts/build-entries.ts && vp pack`) propagated the fix.

`docs:api` now reports 0 errors and 0 warnings. `docs/api` is git-ignored, so nothing there is tracked churn — but note the rebuild did update tracked files under `renderers/web-components/dist/` and `generated/`. Those are legitimately regenerated build artifacts reflecting the comment change.

One thing worth flagging: I made a judgment call to de-link `ELEMENTS` rather than add an `externalSymbolLinkMappings` entry (which the warning suggests). Mapping would only let angular point at a placeholder `#` anchor, so inline text is cleaner. If you'd rather keep `ELEMENTS` as a clickable link in the web-components docs and map it for angular instead, say so and I'll switch approaches.

content.content:
# Publishing to GitHub Packages

This page describes publishing to **GitHub Packages registry** (npm.pkg.github.com), not the public npmjs.com registry.

## The "repository" field

The page emphasizes that the `repository` field links your package to a GitHub repository. When you publish a package with a repository field in `package.json`, the package automatically inherits the repository's access permissions and appears in that repository's Packages section.

The guidance states: "You can connect a package to a repository as soon as the package is published by including a `repository` field in the `package.json` file."

## Publishing multiple packages to the same repository

For multiple packages linked to one repository, the page advises:

"To publish multiple packages and link them to the same repository, you can include the URL of the GitHub repository in the `repository` field of the `package.json` file for each package."

The format should be:

```
"repository":"https://github.com/OWNER/REPOSITORY"
```

The key takeaway: use the same repository URL across all package.json files, and GitHub Packages will match them to that repository automatically.

Based on the search results, the issue you're describing aligns with a known behavior in GitHub. Here's what I found:

## Key Findings

GitHub Packages only supports scoped npm packages, and scoped packages have names with the format of @owner/name and always begin with an @ symbol.

The reason your GitHub repository's Packages sidebar only shows GitHub Packages (and not npm public registry packages) is because if the package name is not scoped, GitHub won't link it to your registry. This is a limitation by design—GitHub Packages specifically filters for scoped packages.

## What You Can Do

To work with both registries, you can add an .npmrc file to your project so all requests to install packages go through GitHub Packages, which allows you to use both scoped and unscoped packages from npmjs.org. However, this affects installation behavior rather than what appears in the GitHub sidebar.

The sidebar display limitation appears to be a feature of how GitHub surfaces packages—it's designed to show packages specifically published to GitHub Packages, not packages from external registries like npm.

...

const EXPECTED_REPOSITORY_URL = "git+https://github.com/thedannywahl/pantoken.git";

input.prompt: For publishing an npm package to GitHub Packages (npm.pkg.github.com): does the package's scope/namespace (@NAMESPACE) have to match the GitHub user or organization that owns the repository? Quote exactly what the docs say about the scope needing to match the account/organization name. Can a package scoped @foo be published to GitHub Packages under a repository owned by a user named "bar"?

content.content:
Based on the documentation provided, there's no explicit statement requiring the package scope to match the repository owner's name.

The docs explain that "Scoped packages have names with the format of `@NAMESPACE/PACKAGE-NAME`" and that you should "replace `NAMESPACE` with the name of the user or organization account to which the package will be scoped." However, this describes what the namespace represents—not a requirement that it must match the repository owner.

The example given shows: if you're the user `octocat` with a package named `test`, you'd use `@octocat/test`. But this is presented as a naming convention example, not a hard rule.

**To answer your specific question:** The documentation doesn't explicitly prohibit publishing a package scoped `@foo` under a repository owned by user `bar`. However, the docs don't clarify whether this is actually possible either. Based on what's written, the scope represents the account associated with the package itself—which may or may not need to align with the repository owner. You'd need to test this or consult GitHub's support to confirm whether mismatched scopes are allowed.

## The Core Issue

The organization name and the package scope must match exactly. When they don't, you'll get publishing errors.

## Common Causes

1. **Scope mismatch**: The scope for a package should match the owner of the repository when publishing to a user account. If you're publishing to an organization, the scope must match that organization name.

2. **Case sensitivity**: GitHub usernames may have uppercase letters while npm scoped package names must be lowercase, creating a casing mismatch between the .npmrc file and the scope used by npm publish.

# Add npm metadata (`repository.directory`, `homepage`, `bugs`) to all publishable packages

## Context

The GitHub repo homepage shows "No packages published" in its Packages sidebar. The original hunch
was that adding a `repository` field to each package.json would fix it. Investigation showed two
things:

1. **`repository` is already present** on all 69 publishable packages (identical
   `git+https://github.com/thedannywahl/pantoken.git`), and it's enforced by a publish gate. The
   sidebar is still empty — proof `repository` isn't what populates it.
2. The GitHub "Packages" sidebar only surfaces packages published to **GitHub Packages**
   (npm.pkg.github.com), never npmjs.com. Publishing there would require the package scope to match
   the repo owner (`thedannywahl`), but the packages are `@pantoken/*` — so it would need a new
   `pantoken` GitHub org + repo move. Out of scope by decision.

So the sidebar can't be fixed by a package.json change, and we're **not** pursuing the GitHub-org
route. What we ARE doing (user-chosen): enrich the npmjs.com metadata so every package page
deep-links to its exact monorepo folder and shows Homepage and Issues links. This is real value,
independent of the sidebar.

**Target metadata for every publishable package:**
- `repository.directory` = the package's repo-relative path (e.g. `formats/css`)
- `homepage` = `https://pantoken.iywahl.com` (docs site root, same for all — user choice)
- `bugs` = `https://github.com/thedannywahl/pantoken/issues`
- `repository.url` stays exactly `git+https://github.com/thedannywahl/pantoken.git` (unchanged; still required for npm OIDC provenance)

## Scope

69 publishable packages: every non-private `@pantoken/*` package (the `isPublishablePackage` rule).
The 4 private `tools/*`/`docs` packages and the private repo-root `pantoken` package are excluded.

## Implementation

There is no template/generator — metadata is duplicated literally per file. Reuse the existing
release tooling rather than hand-editing 69 files.

### 1. Shared constants module — `scripts/release/repository-metadata.ts` (new)

Single source of truth so the writer and the gate can't drift. Export:
- `REPOSITORY_URL` (move the existing constant here), `HOMEPAGE_URL`, `BUGS_URL`.
- `expectedRepository(pkgPath)` → `{ type: "git", url: REPOSITORY_URL, directory: pkgPath }`.

### 2. Writer — `scripts/release/sync-repository-metadata.ts` (new, committed & reusable)

- Load packages with `loadWorkspacePackages()` + `isPublishablePackage()` from
  [scripts/release/workspace-packages.ts](scripts/release/workspace-packages.ts) — `pkg.path` is
  already the POSIX relative dir to use as `directory`.
- For each package.json: parse, set `repository` to `expectedRepository(pkg.path)`, and insert
  `homepage`/`bugs` **immediately after `repository`** by rebuilding the key order (keeps diffs
  localized instead of appending at the end).
- Write with `JSON.stringify(pkg, null, 2) + "\n"` (matches the aggregator's style in
  [tools/aggregate/src/index.ts](tools/aggregate/src/index.ts) and existing files).
- Wire a root script `"sync:repository"` for future re-runs when packages are added.

### 3. Extend the gate — `scripts/release/check-repository-metadata.ts`

Import the shared constants. In addition to the current `repository.url` check, assert per package:
`repository.directory === pkg.path`, `homepage === HOMEPAGE_URL`, `bugs === BUGS_URL`. Keep the
same violation-list + non-zero-exit pattern. This keeps the fields correct on every future publish
via the existing `gate:repository` → `check:publish` wiring in
[vite.config.ts](vite.config.ts).

### Representative files touched

New: `scripts/release/repository-metadata.ts`, `scripts/release/sync-repository-metadata.ts`.
Edited: `scripts/release/check-repository-metadata.ts`, root `package.json` (add `sync:repository`),
and all 69 publishable `package.json` (via the writer) — e.g. `packages/core/package.json`,
`formats/css/package.json`, `renderers/web-components/package.json`, `plugins/vite/*/package.json`,
and the meta package `packages/pantoken/package.json`.

## Verification

1. Run the writer once: `vp exec node scripts/release/sync-repository-metadata.ts` (confirm exact
   invocation against `docs/conventions/build-and-docs.md` — use `vp`, never raw pnpm/node-in-script).
2. Spot-check diffs on a shallow and a deep package (`packages/core`, `plugins/vite/*`) and the meta
   package (`packages/pantoken`): `directory` matches the folder, `homepage`/`bugs` present,
   `repository.url` unchanged, 2-space indent + trailing newline, minimal localized diff.
3. Run the extended gate: `vp run check:repository` (or `gate:repository`) → passes for all 69.
4. Confirm the meta-package aggregator preserves the new fields: it only rewrites `exports`
   ([tools/aggregate/src/index.ts](tools/aggregate/src/index.ts)), but run its aggregate task and
   re-check `packages/pantoken/package.json` still has `homepage`/`bugs`/`directory`.
5. Run the broader gate the fields feed into: `vp run check:publish` (covers `gate:repository` +
   `publint` + `attw`) — `publint` validates field shapes, so it catches a malformed `bugs`/`repository`.
6. Optional: `vp fmt` on the changed package.json (oxc handles JSON) to confirm no formatting drift.

## Explicitly NOT doing

- No GitHub Packages / GitHub-org / repo-move work — that's the only thing that would populate the
  sidebar, and it's declined for now.
- Not changing `repository.url` or any package's scope/name.

# Restyle CdnPicker.vue with InstUI component classes

## Context

The CDN guide page (`docs/guide/cdn.md`) mounts an interactive combine-URL builder,
`CdnPicker.vue`. Today that component is styled with a bespoke `<style scoped>` block using
BEM class names (`.cdn-picker__*`) and raw VitePress theme variables (`--vp-c-*`). The docs
site already loads the full `@pantoken/components` sheet plus the utilities sheet in its theme
entry, so every `instui-*` class is available globally. The picker is the one interactive widget
on the CDN guide, and it currently looks like generic VitePress chrome rather than InstUI.

Goal: rebuild the picker's markup on the shipped InstUI component classes so it reads as an
InstUI surface — matching the look documented in `docs/guide/components.md` — while keeping all
existing behavior (selection state, combine-URL generation, copy, localized strings) unchanged.

## What's available (already loaded in the docs theme)

`docs/.vitepress/theme/index.ts` imports `generated/components.css` (the full component barrel,
including `instui-checkbox`, `instui-radio`, `instui-radio-input-group`, `instui-button`,
`instui-form-field-group`) and `formats/components/generated/utilities.css` (`instui-view`,
`instui-bg-*`, `instui-p-*`/`instui-m-*`, `instui-border-*`, `instui-elevation-*`,
`instui-text`, `instui-heading`). No new imports are needed — this is a template + scoped-CSS
edit only. Reference markup lives in `docs/guide/components.md`.

## Class mapping (behavior stays identical)

Single file: `docs/.vitepress/theme/components/CdnPicker.vue`. Only the `<template>` and
`<style scoped>` change; the `<script setup>` is untouched.

| Current | New |
| --- | --- |
| `.cdn-picker` container | `instui-view` + `instui-bg-secondary` + `instui-p-md` + `instui-border-radius-lg` + `instui-elevation-card` (a real InstUI view surface) |
| `.cdn-picker__group` `<fieldset><legend>` | `instui-form-field-group` (native fieldset/legend, InstUI-styled legend) |
| `.cdn-picker__all` + grid `<label class="cdn-picker__check">` | `<label class="instui-checkbox">` (control-first markup already matches) |

| include-base checkbox | `instui-checkbox` (kept beside the format group) |

# Add npm metadata (`repository.directory`, `homepage`, `bugs`) to all publishable packages

## Context

The GitHub repo homepage shows "No packages published" in its Packages sidebar. The original hunch
was that adding a `repository` field to each package.json would fix it. Investigation showed two
things:

1. **`repository` is already present** on all 69 publishable packages (identical
   `git+https://github.com/thedannywahl/pantoken.git`), and it's enforced by a publish gate. The
   sidebar is still empty — proof `repository` isn't what populates it.
2. The GitHub "Packages" sidebar only surfaces packages published to **GitHub Packages**
   (npm.pkg.github.com), never npmjs.com. Publishing there would require the package scope to match
   the repo owner (`thedannywahl`), but the packages are `@pantoken/*` — so it would need a new
   `pantoken` GitHub org + repo move. Out of scope by decision.

So the sidebar can't be fixed by a package.json change, and we're **not** pursuing the GitHub-org
route. What we ARE doing (user-chosen): enrich the npmjs.com metadata so every package page
deep-links to its exact monorepo folder and shows Homepage and Issues links. This is real value,
independent of the sidebar.

**Target metadata for every publishable package:**
- `repository.directory` = the package's repo-relative path (e.g. `formats/css`)
- `homepage` = `https://pantoken.iywahl.com` (docs site root, same for all — user choice)
- `bugs` = `https://github.com/thedannywahl/pantoken/issues`
- `repository.url` stays exactly `git+https://github.com/thedannywahl/pantoken.git` (unchanged; still required for npm OIDC provenance)

## Scope

69 publishable packages: every non-private `@pantoken/*` package (the `isPublishablePackage` rule).
The 4 private `tools/*`/`docs` packages and the private repo-root `pantoken` package are excluded.

## Implementation

There is no template/generator — metadata is duplicated literally per file. Reuse the existing
release tooling rather than hand-editing 69 files.

### 1. Shared constants module — `scripts/release/repository-metadata.ts` (new)

Single source of truth so the writer and the gate can't drift. Export:
- `REPOSITORY_URL` (move the existing constant here), `HOMEPAGE_URL`, `BUGS_URL`.
- `expectedRepository(pkgPath)` → `{ type: "git", url: REPOSITORY_URL, directory: pkgPath }`.

### 2. Writer — `scripts/release/sync-repository-metadata.ts` (new, committed & reusable)

- Load packages with `loadWorkspacePackages()` + `isPublishablePackage()` from
  [scripts/release/workspace-packages.ts](scripts/release/workspace-packages.ts) — `pkg.path` is
  already the POSIX relative dir to use as `directory`.
- For each package.json: parse, set `repository` to `expectedRepository(pkg.path)`, and insert
  `homepage`/`bugs` **immediately after `repository`** by rebuilding the key order (keeps diffs
  localized instead of appending at the end).
- Write with `JSON.stringify(pkg, null, 2) + "\n"` (matches the aggregator's style in
  [tools/aggregate/src/index.ts](tools/aggregate/src/index.ts) and existing files).
- Wire a root script `"sync:repository"` for future re-runs when packages are added.

### 3. Extend the gate — `scripts/release/check-repository-metadata.ts`

Import the shared constants. In addition to the current `repository.url` check, assert per package:
`repository.directory === pkg.path`, `homepage === HOMEPAGE_URL`, `bugs === BUGS_URL`. Keep the
same violation-list + non-zero-exit pattern. This keeps the fields correct on every future publish
via the existing `gate:repository` → `check:publish` wiring in
[vite.config.ts](vite.config.ts).

### Representative files touched

New: `scripts/release/repository-metadata.ts`, `scripts/release/sync-repository-metadata.ts`.
Edited: `scripts/release/check-repository-metadata.ts`, root `package.json` (add `sync:repository`),
and all 69 publishable `package.json` (via the writer) — e.g. `packages/core/package.json`,
`formats/css/package.json`, `renderers/web-components/package.json`, `plugins/vite/*/package.json`,
and the meta package `packages/pantoken/package.json`.

## Verification

1. Run the writer once: `vp exec node scripts/release/sync-repository-metadata.ts` (confirm exact
   invocation against `docs/conventions/build-and-docs.md` — use `vp`, never raw pnpm/node-in-script).
2. Spot-check diffs on a shallow and a deep package (`packages/core`, `plugins/vite/*`) and the meta
   package (`packages/pantoken`): `directory` matches the folder, `homepage`/`bugs` present,
   `repository.url` unchanged, 2-space indent + trailing newline, minimal localized diff.
3. Run the extended gate: `vp run check:repository` (or `gate:repository`) → passes for all 69.
4. Confirm the meta-package aggregator preserves the new fields: it only rewrites `exports`
   ([tools/aggregate/src/index.ts](tools/aggregate/src/index.ts)), but run its aggregate task and
   re-check `packages/pantoken/package.json` still has `homepage`/`bugs`/`directory`.
5. Run the broader gate the fields feed into: `vp run check:publish` (covers `gate:repository` +
   `publint` + `attw`) — `publint` validates field shapes, so it catches a malformed `bugs`/`repository`.
6. Optional: `vp fmt` on the changed package.json (oxc handles JSON) to confirm no formatting drift.

## Explicitly NOT doing

- No GitHub Packages / GitHub-org / repo-move work — that's the only thing that would populate the
  sidebar, and it's declined for now.
- Not changing `repository.url` or any package's scope/name.

# Enrich + harden package.json metadata across all publishable packages

## Context

The GitHub repo homepage shows "No packages published." The original hunch — add a `repository`
field — turned out to be a non-fix: all 68 publishable packages already carry `repository` (enforced
by a gate), yet the sidebar stays empty. That sidebar only surfaces packages published to **GitHub
Packages** (npm.pkg.github.com), never npmjs.com, and publishing there would require a `pantoken`
GitHub org + repo move (the `@pantoken/*` scope must match the repo owner). We are **not** doing that.

Instead — and since a codemod will touch every package.json anyway — we're enriching the npmjs.com
metadata and hardening the publish gate so the fields can't regress. All decisions below are
user-confirmed.

## Target state for every publishable package (68 packages)

Add / normalize:
- `repository.directory` = the package's repo-relative path (e.g. `formats/css`); `repository.url`
  stays `git+https://github.com/thedannywahl/pantoken.git` (unchanged — still required for npm OIDC provenance).
- `homepage` = `https://pantoken.iywahl.com` (docs site root, same for all).
- `bugs` = `https://github.com/thedannywahl/pantoken/issues`.
- `sideEffects` = `["**/*.css"]` for the **23 CSS-shipping** packages, `false` for the **45** others.
- `engines` = `{ "node": ">=22.18.0" }` (mirrors the repo root).
- `publishConfig.provenance` = `true` (merged into the existing `{ "access": "public" }`).

Not doing: `author` (skipped by choice), `keywords` (not codemod-friendly), any scope/URL change.

**CSS-shipping set (sideEffects `["**/*.css"]`), classified by `.css` in `exports`/`files`:**
`@pantoken/{components,css,angular,astro,bootstrap,css-in-js,docusaurus,foundation,mui,pendo,react,shadcn,storybook,svelte,vitepress,vue,web-components,demo}`
and `@pantoken/plugin-{logos,primitives,stacking,transition,visual-debug}`. All others → `false`.

## Implementation

No template/generator exists — metadata is duplicated literally per file. Reuse the release tooling.

### 1. Shared source of truth — `scripts/release/repository-metadata.ts` (new)

So the writer and the gate can never drift. Export:
- Constants: `REPOSITORY_URL` (move from the gate), `HOMEPAGE_URL`, `BUGS_URL`, `ENGINES` (`{ node: ">=22.18.0" }`).
- `expectedRepository(pkgPath)` → `{ type: "git", url: REPOSITORY_URL, directory: pkgPath }`.
- `expectsCssSideEffects(pkgDir)` → true if the package's `exports`/`files` reference `.css`;
  `expectedSideEffects(pkgDir)` → `["**/*.css"]` or `false`. This is the single classifier both the
  writer and gate call, so a new CSS package is handled and verified identically.

### 2. Writer — `scripts/release/sync-repository-metadata.ts` (new, committed + reusable)

- Load with `loadWorkspacePackages()` + `isPublishablePackage()` from
  [scripts/release/workspace-packages.ts](scripts/release/workspace-packages.ts); `pkg.path` is the
  POSIX relative dir used verbatim as `directory`.
- Per package.json: set `repository` = `expectedRepository(pkg.path)`; set `sideEffects`,
  `engines`, `homepage`, `bugs`; merge `provenance: true` into `publishConfig`. Insert new top-level
  keys **adjacent to `repository`** (rebuild key order) to keep diffs localized.
- Write `JSON.stringify(pkg, null, 2) + "\n"` (matches existing files + the aggregator in
  [tools/aggregate/src/index.ts](tools/aggregate/src/index.ts)).
- Add root script `"sync:repository"` for re-runs when packages are added.

### 3. Harden the gate — `scripts/release/check-repository-metadata.ts`

Import the shared module. Keep the current `repository.url` check and add, per publishable package:
- `repository.directory === pkg.path`, `homepage === HOMEPAGE_URL`, `bugs === BUGS_URL`.
- `sideEffects` deep-equals `expectedSideEffects(pkg.path)`.
- `engines` deep-equals `ENGINES`; `publishConfig.provenance === true`.
- Regression insurance on the already-consistent fields: `license === "MIT"`, `type === "module"`,
  non-empty `files` array, non-empty `description`.

Same violation-list + non-zero-exit pattern. This runs on PRs via the existing `repository` CI job
(`gate:repository` → `check:publish`, wired in [vite.config.ts](vite.config.ts)), so drift is caught
before release.

### Files touched

New: `scripts/release/repository-metadata.ts`, `scripts/release/sync-repository-metadata.ts`.
Edited: `scripts/release/check-repository-metadata.ts`, root `package.json` (add `sync:repository`),
all 68 publishable `package.json` (via the writer) — e.g. `packages/core/package.json` (→ `false`),
`formats/css/package.json` (→ `["**/*.css"]`), `renderers/web-components/package.json`
(→ `["**/*.css"]`), `plugins/vite/*/package.json`, and the meta package `packages/pantoken/package.json`.

## Verification

1. Run the writer once via `vp` (confirm exact invocation against `docs/conventions/build-and-docs.md`).
2. **`sideEffects` correctness (highest-risk field):**
   - Confirm every CSS package got `["**/*.css"]` and no CSS package got `false` (a wrong `false`
     silently drops styles in consumer bundles).
   - For the `false` set, grep each entry module for import-time side effects (top-level calls, global
     mutation); if any package auto-runs on import, list those files instead of `false`. Pay attention
     to `@pantoken/web-components` (gets `["**/*.css"]`, but its `register()` is an explicit call — no
     import-time effect, so tree-shaking its JS is safe) and the meta `@pantoken/pantoken` (verify its
     `.css` subpath exports, if any, aren't tree-shaken away).
3. Spot-check diffs on a shallow, a deep, and the meta package: `directory` matches the folder,
   new fields present, `repository.url` unchanged, 2-space + trailing newline, localized diff.
4. `vp run check:repository` (`gate:repository`) → passes for all 68 with the new assertions.
5. Confirm the meta-package aggregator preserves the new fields — it only rewrites `exports`
   ([tools/aggregate/src/index.ts](tools/aggregate/src/index.ts)); run its aggregate task and re-check
   `packages/pantoken/package.json` still has every added field.
6. `vp run check:publish` (covers `gate:repository` + `publint` + `attw`); `publint` validates field
   shapes, catching a malformed `bugs`/`sideEffects`/`engines`.
7. Optional: `vp fmt` on changed package.json (oxc handles JSON) to confirm no formatting drift.

## Explicitly NOT doing

- No GitHub Packages / GitHub-org / repo-move — the only thing that would populate the sidebar, declined.
- No `author`/`keywords`; no change to any package's scope, name, or `repository.url`.

# Add npm metadata (`repository.directory`, `homepage`, `bugs`) to all publishable packages

## Context

The GitHub repo homepage shows "No packages published" in its Packages sidebar. The original hunch
was that adding a `repository` field to each package.json would fix it. Investigation showed two
things:

1. **`repository` is already present** on all 69 publishable packages (identical
   `git+https://github.com/thedannywahl/pantoken.git`), and it's enforced by a publish gate. The
   sidebar is still empty — proof `repository` isn't what populates it.
2. The GitHub "Packages" sidebar only surfaces packages published to **GitHub Packages**
   (npm.pkg.github.com), never npmjs.com. Publishing there would require the package scope to match
   the repo owner (`thedannywahl`), but the packages are `@pantoken/*` — so it would need a new
   `pantoken` GitHub org + repo move. Out of scope by decision.

So the sidebar can't be fixed by a package.json change, and we're **not** pursuing the GitHub-org
route. What we ARE doing (user-chosen): enrich the npmjs.com metadata so every package page
deep-links to its exact monorepo folder and shows Homepage and Issues links. This is real value,
independent of the sidebar.
